title: I/O addressing and tags
summary: PLC programs refer to I/O by addresses or symbolic tags. The hardware configuration ties a module channel to an address; the program ties the address to a meaningful name.

sections.heading: Address styles
sections.body:
| Style | Example | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IEC direct address | `%IX0.0`, `%QX0.0`, `%IW64` | IEC 61131-3, many CODESYS-based systems |
| Byte.bit process image | `%I0.0`, `%Q0.1`, `%IW64` | Siemens S7 |
| Module-defined tags | `Local:1:I.Data.0` | Rockwell Logix |
| Linked variables | variable linked to a terminal channel | Beckhoff TwinCAT |
| Device addresses | `X0`, `Y0` (octal on FX) | Mitsubishi MELSEC |

sections.heading: Symbolic programming
sections.body: Modern projects program almost exclusively with **tags** (StartPB, LevelRaw). The address only appears in the I/O mapping. In PLC Lab the hardware view shows, for each channel, the address in the style of the selected platform profile and the tag mapped to it.

sections.heading: Start addresses
sections.body: Each module occupies an address range that starts at its configured **start address**. Moving a module to another slot, or changing its start address, changes all its addresses; programs that use tags survive this, programs that use absolute addresses break.
